title: Practice
tagline: Abhyasa — steady effort, day after day
description: Learn the secrets of sustainable progress by understanding how to establish a practice that is grounded, consistent, and long-lasting.

sutra.meaning: Repeated practice without atachment is the way to still the mind

sections.insight: Consistency and letting go brings mastery. I will not be focused on the end result while I practice regularly.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I practice consistently without constantly measuring my progress?
sections.practice: Do a single task during the day with full attention

मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
sections.wisdomFrom:
You have right to action only, 
never to fruits. Let not the
 fruits of action be thy motive,

sections.gurudevInsight: this is all mind stuff, more & more you are aware of it & then that is it, it just vanishes, that is abhyasa, this is practice. Next sutra: Sa tu dirghkaal nairantarya satkarsevito drudbhoomi This effort to be steady,the effort to be still is practice. For a moment you realize, this is this moment & then that vanishes from your sight. But the moment you have said now, then again you have lost the now. It’s not right to say you have lost but in some sense you feel you are not in the now. But this effort to be established steadily in the now, because the now is not just linear, the now is very deep & vast. [PDF p.13]

sutra.meaning: Practice becomes firm when done for a long time with sincerity and dedication.

sections.insight:
Consistency builds strength physically, mentally and of character, naturally. 
I need to honour the practice and do it with complete faith and commitment.
sections.reflectionPrompt: What practice can I sustain daily?
sections.practice: Repeat one practice daily with total commitment.

sutra.meaning:
Detachment is freedom from craving
Complete detachment comes from self-realization

sections.insight:
Letting go reduces disturbance and restlessness of the mind. Clinging to what has already passed is a habit and can be overcome with meditation.
Deep freedom arises from knowing the self.
sections.reflectionPrompt:
What am I attached to?
What can I release today?
sections.practice:
Observe persistent desires and cravings.
Practice surrender
sections.journalPrompt:
Where did I cling?
What did I release?
sections.gurudevInsight: That is the purpose of practice & how can that be achieved? It takes long time (dirghkaal), without a Gap (nairantarya), with Honour & with Respect (satkarsevito) receiving it & practicing it then it becomes firmly established (drudbhoomi). Anything in life that is of some value takes some time to culture. To master an art, whether its cooking or playing a guitar, sitar, synthesizer, flute, it takes some time, isn’t it? Though it is the same fingers but in flute you have to use the fingers for a while.You cannot say in one day you learn the flute. Its not possible to learn an instrument in one day. [PDF p.13]

sutra.meaning: Practice and detachment can make one experience samadhi in four ways- i) self-analysis, wherein one logically understands the 'Self' and experiences a shift within. ii) synthesis of senses and thought which brings about 'an awareness' without any disturbance iii) bliss iv) only the experience of 'I am'

sections.insight: It can be a gradual movement from one to the other or any one of the ways.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I need to rationally understand the process or am I willing to sit for meditation and let go?
sections.practice: Meditation evolves gradually, give yourself time. Be patient but not slack.
sections.meditation: sit in meditation for 10 mins and observe your experience
sections.journalPrompt: What do I feel in silence?
sections.gurudevInsight: Suddenly white light coming down – they say Oh!, Something has come down, something is happening – people get misled by such experiences, such evangelic experiences. All this evangelic experiences you should know they are all from sanskara sheshas, some sanskaras from the past, that is a different type of samadhi, hmm. (10) “Bhavpratyayo videha prakrutilayanaam” this goes more into an esoteric life. Samadhi is not a property of just this level of existence. People who do not have body, they too can get affected by the Meditation. [PDF p.21]

sutra.meaning:
Intense effort brings quick progress
Effort varies in intensity -i) feeble ii) moderate iii)steady

sections.insight: Depth of desire determines growth. Focussed effort with absolute faith in yourself, the process and the teacher brings quick results. Ultimately the pace of growth depends on your effort.
sections.reflectionPrompt:
How strong is my intention?
Where am I on this scale?
sections.practice:
Act with intensity in all you do today.
Observe effort level

sections.practice: Be 100% present in whatever you do today

sutra.meaning:
The Chitta ie consciousness should be totaly focused and surrendered to God.
Ishvara is untouched by suffering and karma.

sections.insight: The divine is pure and unaffected. To reach that state commensurate effort is required.
sections.gurudevInsight: Now Patanjali in the next sutra very beautifully analyzes, what is that state of consciousness? That consciousness is free from misery or suffering. Kleshakarmavipakashayerparamrusta purushvishesh ishwara. That core of consciousness, which is free from suffering. Five types of sufferings he enunciates 1. Ignorance: - When your consciousness is filled with ignorance, then there is restlessness, there is unhappiness, suffering. [PDF p.26]

sutra.meaning: Complete surrender to the Divine with the repetition of the Aum removes obstacles to the mastery of the inner self

sections.insight: Inner connection ie. when the experiencer, the experience and the experienced become one there is no inner or outer turmoil.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I able to go inwards when I sit in silence with eyes closed?
sections.practice: Observe your thoughts. Does that quieten them
sections.gurudevInsight: So alive & full of prana & all the 31 obstacles gets removed from your way. Just the memory of the Lordship, of the Divine can remove obstacles from your way. “Vyadhisathyaanasanshaypranadaalasyaviratibrantidarshanalabhdabhoomitvanavasth itatva” 1) Vyadhi means illness in the body is one obstacle, first obstacle. 2) Sathyaana: Illness of the mind, second obstacle. Mentally retarded, inability to comprehend, to listen, understand, follow, practice, do anything. You know many of you’ll be all right but when you get on the course sometimes you get sick. [PDF p.32]

sutra.meaning: Focused awareness on one object stabilizes the mind.

sections.insight: Attention brings stability in mind and body.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I keep my complete attention on the job at hand?
sections.gurudevInsight: “Prachardanvidharanbhya va pranasya” In a special manner modulating the prana & the breath. By this also your mind becomes calm & one pointed, one focused, hmm! Another Sutra: “vishayvati va pravrutirutpanna manastithinibandhani” Suppose this doesn’t work, it does work but if you feel that still little incompletion is there, then through any one object of senses, the mind can be stilled, you are gazing, what is happening in gazing? You are looking at somebody, for a few moments, you gaze from all your heart, your mind that time is not running here & there. [PDF p.40]

sutra.meaning:
Om is the expression of the divine
Repeat Om with awareness

sections.insight:
Sound connects to consciousness.
Repetition deepens experience.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I feel the vibrations of the sounds around me?
sections.practice: Chant Om 11 times watching the vibrations it makes within
sections.gurudevInsight: Whatever the master is, it is nothing but the core of your Being. & it is the same as the Divine that rules this entire creation. “Sa purveshamapi guru kaalenaanvachedaat” This Being, consciousness is the guru, is the guide even to the ones who were before. There is no breakage of time as far as it is concerned. I think there was something in Bible – I was before Abraham. Same thing Krishna also says, he say’s I have taught to Ishwaku & Manu. [PDF p.29]

sutra.meaning:
The mind becomes clarified and serene by cultivating: 
Maitri (Friendliness) toward those who are happy,
Karuṇa (Compassion) toward those who are unhappy or suffering ,
Mudita (Joy) toward those who are virtuous or meritorious and
Upekṣa (Equanimity/Indifference) toward those who are non-virtuous or sinful (apuṇya). 


Or regulating the breath calms the mind too.

sections.insight:
One should be friendly and compassionate to all but be in close proximity to only those who are in a happy state of mind for sad and grumpy people will make you sad and grumpy which will do no favours to you or the person concerned.
Feeling happy for the success of good people and indifferent to that of those who you think dont deserve it is a smart thing to do. Such an attitude will help you maintain your own equanimity.








Breath is the key to balance.
sections.reflectionPrompt: I need to watch my emotional entanglement while dealing with other people. Can I take a step back and observe myself?
sections.practice: Observe your breathing. Inhale full and watch your belly inflate; exhale slowly and see it deflate. Continue for a few mins.
sections.shlokaFrom:
चञ्चलं हि मन: कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् |
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् || 34||
sections.wisdomFrom: The mind is very restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate, O Krishna. It appears to me that it is more difficult to control than the wind.
sections.gurudevInsight: So he says don’t be friendly with unhappy people but be compassionate to them. People who are suffering, have sympathy, compassion for them, but don’t hook on to friendliness because then it drags you down and makes you unhappy. If you are unhappy & they are happy, you will be of no use to help them out. If you think you should share the unhappiness with your friend. Ok, you share it, then, will you be able to share your happiness with them? So, unhappy people - don’t be friendly with them but be compassionate to them. [PDF p.38]

sutra.meaning: Mastery of contemplation gives the power to extend from  the smallest to largest and from the subtlest to the grossest.

sections.insight: Awareness expands limitlessly. Maharishi Patanjali has given various methods of dhyan or meditation  to master ones chitta or cosciousness and stop the desires from overtaking the mind.
sections.reflectionPrompt: How can I expand my awareness?
sections.practice: Observe things and events deeply, down to their very core.
sections.gurudevInsight: And with that unhappy mind, that person gets jittery, angry, tensed, all the other things, negativity comes to them & they get soaked in negativity & they die like that. Patanjali gives this Vishoka va jyotishmati - means get rid of the unhappiness. You look into your mind & when you see oh, this is the sadness, this is simply unfounded, Self made. The moment you look your mind, the Self-made sadness will disappear. It is just a concept like one another concept there could be that people don’t respect me. This is baseless Nobody respects me, I am not smart enough. [PDF p.42]
